In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. title: Receipts/Req2283ReferencedGenericStructTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/2), passes on head (2/2); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1

refutes.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites in TypeCollector: reporter lines 735, 1009 and 1101. Two hunks map to 1009 and 1101 (both offset by 24 lines, now 985/1077). No hunk touches the third site, which would be around line 711 in this file. The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper does not protect that site, because `Diagnostic.Create(..., X.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]...)` arguments are evaluated before the sink is called. If the generator (which may run with a null reportDiagnostic, so the `?.Invoke` sites never evaluate their arguments) reaches that site, the IndexOutOfRangeException and CS8785 remain, and no resolver is produced.
